requirements.title: The lexical-token union admits its listed categories and spellings
requirements.source: 6.2.1 p1, second sentence; J3/24-007 PDF page 68, printed page 54, lines 8-10.
requirements.definition: The program-unit lexical classification admits statement keywords, names, noncomplex literal constants, operators, statement labels, the delimiter category, and the explicitly listed .NIL., comma, =, =>, :, ::, ;, .., ?, and % spellings. A complex literal constant is excluded as a single lexical token, not prohibited as a compound literal. Each alternative still needs a legal enclosing grammar and source form. A named constant uses a name token, not an additional literal category. The = assignment symbol is a separate alternative: it is neither a defined operator nor a member of the delimiter list in 6.2.6.
requirements.oracle: All fourteen programs are positive controls for admission, with finite self-checks supplied by their enclosing constructs. The basic control checks two separately declared and assigned integers. Separate literal controls check a default real, both logical values, a character value containing punctuation, and the integer DATA value of B'101' (5). Further controls check parenthesized integer arithmetic, a forward labeled branch, an in-bounds array section, association with a defined scalar TARGET, two semicolon-separated assignments, a scalar actual argument's rank, and a scalar derived-type component. The question-mark control selects 17 and 29 in separate true/false evaluations. The .NIL. control independently checks optional-argument presence for true/false selections; it accesses the argument only inside a PRESENT guard. All objects read have been defined, no loop is needed, and the absent argument is never evaluated.
requirements.oracle_limitation: This finite union plan does not establish complete canonical name, literal, operator, label, delimiter, or construct semantics. The five literal facets refine just the noncomplex-literal member; no complex-literal rejection is invented. Ordinary valid programs do not reveal the processor's token count or prove the complex-literal exclusion, so that definitional boundary remains source-only. The controls neither exhaust keyword/operator spellings and kinds nor test source-form blank, continuation, or token-boundary rules. Punctuation inside a character literal is not credited as independent punctuation or delimiter tokens. The two F2023 conditional controls are separate from each other and from assumed-rank support; .NIL. nevertheless necessarily depends on conditional-argument syntax. No negative case is allocated: a real diagnostic obligation would have to be justified by the applicable numbered grammar/constraint or Clause 6 source-form/character rule under 4.2 p2(3)/(5), not by treating this classification as a context-free illegal-character blacklist.
requirements.dependencies: 5.5.2 p1 defines the unqualified statement keyword (PDF 65). Canonical ownership stays with 6.2.2 R603/C601, 6.2.3 R604-R607/C602, 6.2.4 R608-R610 and the Clause 10 operator rules, 6.2.5 R611/C603 and prose, and 6.2.6. R605 and 7.4.3.1/R708, 7.4.3.2/R714, 7.4.4.3/R724, 7.4.5/R725, and 7.7/R772-R776 supply the five noncomplex literal categories. R718 and 6.3.2.2 p1 explain the complex-literal boundary (PDF 83 and 71). C7119, 8.6.7 p8/p11, and 16.9.110 p5 case (vi) justify the small, zero-padded BOZ DATA value without a sign-bit assumption (PDF 114, 138, 422). R401/R801, R1033, R1001 and 10.1.3, R1159, R922, R1034 with C1016/C1022/C1024/C1028 and 10.2.2.3 p1-p2, 6.3.2.5 p2, and R911/R913 supply the ordinary punctuation contexts. R827/C839/C840 and 16.9.171 p5 justify the assumed-rank inquiry (PDF 127-128, 449). R1002/C1004 and 10.1.4 p6-p7 justify conditional expressions (PDF 169, 174). R1526-R1528/C1538-C1544, 15.5.2.3 p1-p4, and 16.9.163 justify the optional INTENT(IN) conditional argument and PRESENT guard (PDF 336, 338, 445). 4.2 p2(1) supplies conforming execution; intrinsic assignment remains governed by 10.2.1.3.

accounting.rationale: PDF 68, printed 54, lines 8-10: subdivide the introductory scope, all sixteen lexical-list members, and the explicit complex-literal exception. The subdivisions are semantic accounting, not eighteen new mandatory effects.
The first sentence identifies the low-level syntax's program-unit subject. It adds no separately observable runtime effect or rejection obligation.
Admission of the statement-keyword category; 5.5.2 retains its definition and nonreserved-word rule.
Admission of a name token; R603/C601 remain the canonical spelling and length owners.
The literal member is qualified by the separately accounted complex exclusion. Five admission facets come from R605's other alternatives; this does not duplicate their defining grammars.

The words excluding a complex literal concern one-token classification, not legality of complex literals. R718 describes the compound literal and 6.3.2.2 p1 explicitly permits blanks between its tokens. No ordinary runtime oracle establishes internal token boundaries; no fabricated negative or effect facet is credited.
Preserve .NIL. as its own token, not an operator or logical literal. R1527/C1540 limits the chosen control to a conditional argument corresponding to an optional dummy.
Admission of an operator; 6.2.4 and Clause 10 retain the intrinsic/defined/extended categories and their detailed semantics.
Admission of a statement label in a legal branch context, without reauthoring R611/C603 or the 6.2.5 prose.
Admission of the delimiter category in a parenthesized expression. The seven spellings are accounted in 6.2.6, not redefined here.
The separately enumerated comma is admitted in R801's entity-decl-list under R401.
Preserve the separate = alternative, used by R1033 for assignment. It is not promoted to a defined operator or to a 6.2.6 delimiter.
Preserve => exactly; a same-type, same-kind scalar pointer and defined scalar TARGET provide a legal R1034 context.
The single-colon alternative is admitted in an in-bounds R922 subscript triplet; the detailed triplet constraints remain canonical.
Preserve :: exactly in an R801 declaration separator, separately from the single-colon list member.
A ; separates two free-form assignments. Its statement-termination behavior and character/comment exceptions belong to 6.3.2.5, including that the terminator is not part of the statement.
Preserve .. exactly in an R827 assumed-rank dummy declaration. A RANK inquiry is an allowed use under C840, not an unrestricted expression reference to that dummy.
The ? control uses R1002 conditional expressions with matching scalar integer alternatives, independently of optional arguments and .NIL.
The % control uses R911/R913 to select a declared integer component of a declared scalar derived-type object.

review_rationale: Coordinator review independent of the draft authors; see doc/source_audits/lexical_batch_003.json. All sixteen listed token alternatives, introductory scope, and the complex-literal exception are accounted for. The five noncomplex-literal facets refine one union member. Complex literals are not prohibited, punctuation inside literals is not separately credited, and canonical lexical/construct ownership is unchanged.
